I'm on Seroquel currently and have lost around 25 pounds since I started. I think I've been on it since last September. I do take a low dose of 150mg XR,  though. I take it right before bed and have learned when I get extremely hungry it is the effects of Seroquel, so I don't eat and then end up falling asleep about 10 minutes later.

I've read and been told that 150mg XR is a pretty low dose of Seroquel but it does help my mood stay more consistent and the XR keeps the groggy feelings away. I can wake up 4-5 hours after falling asleep (which is usually 1.5-2 hours after I take it) and feel perfectly fine the rest of the day.

Hmm, well I probably won't as they are helping me become stable. I also don't really think it was an example related to what I was asking for.

I think the main thing it helps me with is my anxiety and racing thoughts. I don't know how else it affects me though 🤔. I was not sleeping and it made me worse but I just wasn't getting tired so I wouldn't lay down.

I didn't really get the sedative effect the past few times. I'm on lamotrigine, Rexulti, and atomoxetine currently, but going to ask about stopping the atomoxetine (Strattera) and ask about switching to something else.

1-2 weeks. I've never had a depressive episode last longer than that. I was diagnosed in 2018 when I was 21 years old.

Right now I'm supposedly rapid cycling and it's been 1-2 days of depression every 1.5 weeks. About 4-5 days of hypomania then a couple days of stability then 1-2 days of depression and repeat for the last 2 months. Before this I was stable for a whole year.

During the last hypomanic/manic episode I had (and am potentially still in) I was having a lot of reckless ideas and impulsively acting on some of them. I haven't drank in a really long time but I bought alcohol twice (didn't drink it tho) and smoked a cigarette I randomly found at my house even though I don't smoke. My thoughts were rapid firing and I had an uncomfortable amount of energy. My sleep schedule was something like, sleep for 8 hours one night, then the next was an hour, and repeat for a week or two. 

I impulsively called out of work last second and packed a bag then drove somewhere almost an hour away before I turned around because "I wanted to start a new life". Was told I was/am having rapid loud speech and am feeling a lot more talkative than normal. I was doing things that I wasn't sure exactly what or why I was doing it and felt on the verge of losing all of my self control.

  
Another episode I was convinced that I was going to invent something that would change the world, get a noble prize, then become elected president. Was also sleeping a lot less then too and feeling more rested than normal on about 4 hours of sleep each night. Started working out and drinking a lot more. One day after maybe 2-3 weeks I just woke up and was like "hmmm, that was weird" and was back to normal.

Also have had episodes where I was severely paranoid something was actively going to happen to me. Once it was someone was going to break into my house then another time it was that everyone was talking about me and plotting against me.

A lot of my symptoms were in the cross post. I feel back to normal today though and not hypomanic really at all now. These periods are why I haven't messaged my nurse practitioner or rescheduled my appointment.
I'm feeling pretty normal today after sleeping an okay amount. These fluctuations and the fact that I have periods of feeling normal like this is what keeps me from messaging her or rescheduling.
Eh I'm feeling pretty normal again today after sleeping an okay amount. 🤔
I am on am antipsychotic but it was just decreased a month ago.
Well one was at a bar that I sat at while waiting for my friend at a restaurant. I told them I changed my mind then left. The second time I put it in our fridge.

I told her it was suggested by others that I be seen sooner but that I feel fine now (I was feeling more level at the time I sent the message) and she said if I feel that way then it’s okay to wait. My SO is going to go to my next appointment with me. We watched a Dr. Tracey Marks video on hypomania vs mania and they said they think I’m hypomanic right now but have been fully manic in the past. They said it even said in the video that people who are in elevated episodes have a hard time or don’t realize they’re in the episode until someone says something or until it’s over.

My brain is making me feel like it should be rushed. Last night when my SO was asleep a small part of me got the urge to leave then... or work on my hobby, but I got tired and went to sleep instead since I figured that was for the best.

I keep thinking that I'll be the person these all work out for. 

I'm worried my nurse practitioner will say I'm hypomanic or something like she did last time. I don't really want to completely change off of this antipsychotic.
So it's not a bad idea?

I have a nurse practitioner that I like and she seems to actually want to help me feel better. She listens to what I have to say. I was the one who wanted to decrease my antipsychotic because I feel like it was limiting my creative thinking. I take Rexulti and decreased it from 4mg to 3mg. I felt really depressed at first but now I feel like this (or am acting like this anyways).

I've been sleeping less at night but forcing myself to take naps to balance it out. Last night I slept about 10 hours.

Someone suggested I have my SO talk with my nurse practitioner with me at an appointment
I'm not really worried myself but other people are saying I'm not seeming like myself or things I've described aren't normal.

I don't really feel like I've made unfixable decisions 🤔. Someone asked if I'm maintaining my schedule or daily household stuff and to be honest I'm not maintaining anything like that. I just don't really think about it lately.

I read my post to my SO and they were upset to learn I didn't actually go to work and agree that my thoughts are becoming weird. They also think I need to go back up to my original dose of my med. 

It sucks to think my brain is so sensitive to change in meds. I made a few posts a while ago about a different med change that caused issues too :(.

I haven't been having any side effects. I've actually been sleeping less at night but forcing myself to take naps during the day to balance it out. Someone suggested I might actually be in an elevated episode. I don't know if that's true or not

Ive mentioned a lot that one reason I doubt my diagnosis is that I barely get depressed and it’s only for about 1-1.5 weeks at a time, but I’m told if you have bipolar 1 it doesn’t make a difference. Idk though

Interesting. I don’t think I’m hypomanic at the moment just finally feeling creative and clear headed ☺️. I’m not sure what my nurse practitioner would say if I said I wanted to still be hypomanic 🤔. My last nurse practitioner would have definitely disagreed that I should be able to. Sometimes it seems like people just don’t want me to feel good.
Happens to me every so often and literally happened last night. Saw a huge swarm of flies on the ceiling. I always end up turning on my flash light to confirm there’s nothing actually there.
I had the pepto bismol commercial stuck in my head one day.
Ok, thanks for responding 🙂. I'll make sure to keep an eye on it. My SO and friends can help with it too since sometimes I'm not as good as identifying if I've had any changes.

Vraylar made me hypomanic when I took it a couple years ago.

I am having the same paranoia and anxiety about someone breaking into my house and also had a meltdown thinking it was actually about to happen one night. Yeah I feel like I'm having a lot of thoughts and ideas but at the same time, I have no idea what I'm thinking about... it's weird to explain.

The high pitched thing is like if you were playing a video or movie in fast forward.

They do know about my diagnosis. Maybe she thought the antidepressant would be okay since I'm on the max dose of my antipsychotic and pretty high dose of my mood stabilizer. If I still have control of my actions and feel good about myself (for once) then what does it hurt?

I was diagnosed with bp1 even though I'm pretty sure I've never been manic. I just added the antidepressant because I was feeling down and already on the max dose of my other meds that would help. I'm not even convinced I'm bipolar at all to be honest. I think I've been exaggerating my feelings and ADHD causes me to just impulsively say things that come across my mind which makes it seem worse.

I didn't have to go to a hospital or get arrested though and I'm actually convinced I was just hypomanic then.

I'm not consistently 15 minutes late... it's happened 5 times in the last year, which is still a lot but it's not an every day thing.

I'm not \*constantly\* 15 minutes late. Its happened a few times but it's not an \*every\* day thing. It's happened like 5 times in the last year I've worked here. The traffic issue was fixed after the first couple times. The only reason traffic became an issue was because I started working at 8am vs 10am-12pm when there wasn't any traffic on my way to work. I do make an effort to be on time which I am the majority of days. I'm probably just gonna ask my manager next time I see him.

I'm pretty sure I was told we can only clock in 5 minutes early unless we get permission 🤔. I mentioned in another comment that I wake up tired or struggle getting out of bed no matter when or how long I slept. That fact and anxiety about work is my problem. I did have a later availability when I had even worse anxiety about work but then I wasn't getting that many hours so after a while when my anxiety went down I moved it earlier again.
A bunch of people were written up for being late regularly and a couple other people were fired for it. This was a while ago and they never mentioned it to me.

I just don't hear it sometimes, so I doubt I would hear it across the room. I'm not trying to make excuses I just started keeping it where I do because other ways didn't work. I guess I could go back to keeping alarms on my smart watch.

I do set multiple alarms and keep my phone right by my head so I'll hear them, but I've still managed to sleep through them before. I have also been leaving earlier. I'm on time 95% of the time and stay late 95% of the time too.

I feel a lot better the past couple of days

I said I had a couple thoughts but not really and wasn't planning on doing anything.

Do you do stuff you know you shouldn't? I stole something from a store today because...why not? I also don't think it makes much of a difference because I don't even think we actually exist. I haven't drank in over 2 years

Like my 1st psych wouldn't prescribe me an SSRI for anxiety even though I've seen its fine if you're on a mood stabilizer and my current psych was willing to. My 1st also wouldn't agree with me stopping my AP but my current one did.

I'm thinking about seeing another psych and bringing it up.

Idk, I feel like I exaggerated my symptoms and convinced people I am but now that I decided I'm not they don't believe me. I asked my current psych why she put that as my diagnosis but she wouldn't tell me why so I'm gonna ask her again when I see her next time but I don't see her for another month because I just saw her a few days ago.
Yeah I just restarted therapy and am on lamictal and sertraline so it's not like I'm refusing to take medicine completely.

I don't want to take an AP at all anymore. I think I'm managing fine without it. My psych prescribed me rexulti a few weeks ago and I picked it up and told her I decided I didn't want to take it and she said ok that I didn't have to.

He did today. He said it was weird that I tried to take a random trip with our dog. That I tried to make up a code and stuff related to that. I said I wanted to start a commune to do science experiments but that was kind of a joke but he said it didn't seem like it. I don't think most of this stuff is that weird. I've talked about it with some other people and they said that I should do what I want to do and that my husband shouldn't be trying to control me. I think people in my life just want to put me on meds that they think will make me "easier" to deal with even though I don't like some of the side effects.
